definitions.explanation: Something happening without intention or planning; coincidentally.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}で{偶々|たまたま}{友達|ともだち}に{会|あ}った。
examples.english: I happened to meet a friend at the station.

examples.japanese: {偶々|たまたま}{通|とお}りかかった{店|みせ}で{買|か}い{物|もの}をした。
examples.english: I shopped at a store I happened to pass by.

examples.japanese: {偶々|たまたま}{見|み}たテレビ{番組|ばんぐみ}が{面白|おもしろ}かった。
examples.english: A TV program I happened to watch was interesting.

notes:
WRITING:
- Usually written in hiragana as たまたま
- Kanji {偶々|たまたま} is less common but may appear in formal writing

SIMILAR WORDS:
- たまたま: By chance (neutral, common)
- {偶然|ぐうぜん}: Coincidentally (slightly more formal)
- {思|おも}いがけず: Unexpectedly (emphasizes surprise)

NUANCE: たまたま is very common in everyday conversation to describe coincidental or unplanned occurrences.
